common_name: Rutgers Obsession Basil (Compact Downy-Mildew-Resistant Purple Basil)

planting.note: Start seed indoors and transplant after all frost danger passes into warm, rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Rutgers Obsession was bred for a compact habit, deep purple color, and strong downy mildew resistance.

directions: Start seed indoors and transplant into warm, rich, well-drained soil in full sun after all frost danger passes. Rutgers Obsession was bred at Rutgers University for deep, uniform purple leaf color, a compact, well-branched habit that fits containers and small garden spaces, and strong resistance to the downy mildew that has become a major problem for basil growers in humid climates. Its purple leaves add striking color contrast to garden beds and containers as well as flavor and color to vinegars, pestos, and garnishes. Pinch growing tips to encourage bushy growth and remove flower buds promptly to keep leaves tender and productive through the season.
sources: Cornell Cooperative Extension — Basil Downy Mildew

common_name: Amethyst Falls Oregano (Trailing Pink Hop-Flowered Ornamental Oregano)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants after the last hard frost in lean, very well-drained soil in full sun; Amethyst Falls is an ornamental trailing oregano similar to Kent Beauty, grown for its cascading pink hop-like flower clusters.

directions: Amethyst Falls is an ornamental oregano hybrid grown for its cascading clusters of overlapping, papery, rose-pink bracts that resemble small hanging hops, held above rounded, gray-green, aromatic leaves on trailing stems. Like its close relative Kent Beauty, it is grown chiefly for its ornamental flower display rather than culinary use, and its trailing habit shows best spilling from a raised bed, rock garden pocket, or hanging container where the pendant flowers can be appreciated up close. Give it lean, very well-drained soil in full sun, since excess moisture and humidity quickly lead to rot, and expect a shorter garden life than culinary oregano, particularly in hot, humid summers.
